terra.problem: The cookie-batch comparison makes light of the serious sin described in the verse.
The claim that there was no gate to slip through conflicts with the men of war fleeing by a gate in 2 Kings 25:4.
The line about the answer being on the other side of the ditch does not make clear sense as a joke or clue.
The text says the men fled by night, not at midnight. It also does not say the Chaldeans surrounded the city the whole time.
Calling the flight a midnight cookie run makes light of a desperate escape and mixes the cookie comparison with the biblical setting.
The text says the Chaldeans pursued and overtook the king. It does not say they were right behind the fleeing men or that the men were creeping.
The claim that nobody gets let go goes beyond the text. It says the king was overtaken and his army deserted him, not what happened to every member of the army.
The passage does not say whether the Chaldeans needed to wait for anyone.
The claim that no one is let go goes beyond the passage, which also says some of the poorest were left in the land.
The verse does not say whether any nobles stayed behind; it says some of the poorest were left to tend the land.
The joke about taking a bow sits on the taking away of priests and doorkeepers, making light of a serious moment.
The passage says some of the poorest were left to tend the fields, but does not say they were the only people left to work them.
